The racism?
It's because against Indigenous people they don't consider it racism.
I didn't want to be president.
The Brazilian voter really is unpredictable.
Is there no way at all for me to get stripped of office?
Talk about animals.

meanings.note: First-person singular possessive agreeing with the thing possessed.

examples.text: O seu tempo vale mais que o meu?
examples.trans: Is your time worth more than mine?

meanings.note: Always plural in form; Meus parabéns! means Congratulations!
Links verbs like faltar to an event or destination.
Agrees in gender and number; before an adjective (todo travado) means completely.

examples.text: A culpa toda disso foi dele.
examples.trans: All the blame for this was his.
I am all locked up in my neck.

meanings.note: Subject form referring to the speaker. Explicit eu introduces his department in the explanation.
Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.
Irregular participle of eleger; agrees in gender and number with the person elected.

examples.text: Ele foi eleito no primeiro turno.
examples.trans: He was elected in the first round.

meanings.note: Elected representative in the state assembly or federal Chamber of Deputies.

examples.text: Eu fui eleita deputada mais votada.
examples.trans: I was elected the most-voted congresswoman.

meanings.note: Marks comparisons (mais que), negated continuation (não ... mais, not anymore), and the farewell até mais.
In the superlative a mais votada, designates the candidate who received the highest vote total.

examples.trans: I was the most-voted city councilor.

examples.text: Ele foi o deputado mais votado.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
Used with a or para/pra for reaching a destination.

examples.text: Só pra chegar e comprar um pão.
examples.trans: Just to get there and buy a roll.

meanings.note: Informal reduced para. Before a feminine noun, this Brazilian spelling can also represent a contraction including the article a; the exact meeting is clear from context.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Stressed 1st-person singular pronoun used after prepositions like para/pra, de, sem.

examples.trans: That is enough for me, I am leaving.
Did you bring a coffee for me?

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.
Standard political verb for resigning from elected office.

examples.text: Chega pra mim, eu vou renunciar.
examples.trans: That is enough for me, I am going to resign.

meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Covers speaking, talking, and telling in everyday Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?

meanings.note: Very frequent general noun; singular muita coisa naturally translates as a lot of things.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Entalado na garganta describes words or feelings stuck in someone's throat waiting to come out.

examples.trans: That was stuck in the throat.
I had the shout stuck in my throat.

meanings.note: Usually contracts with definite articles to no, na, nos, nas.
Entalado na garganta literally means stuck in one's throat (something people were dying to say).

examples.trans: That was stuck in the throat.

meanings.note: Often used in the singular (o eleitor brasileiro) to refer collectively to the typical voter.

examples.text: Os eleitores vão às urnas domingo.
examples.trans: Voters go to the polls on Sunday.

meanings.note: Refers to the state of São Paulo and its voters; same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: The São Paulo voter voted for her.
The São Paulo economy is strong.

meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Initial r- is pronounced [ʁ] and the s before m is voiced [z].
Written as one word without an accent in answers and explanations.

examples.text: Estou aqui porque venderam o apartamento.
examples.trans: I am here because they sold the apartment.

examples.text: Porque ninguém tem fé na gente.
examples.trans: Because nobody has faith in us.

meanings.note: Marks accompaniment or an added ingredient such as sweetener.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.

meanings.note: Traditional everyday term for an Indigenous person in Brazil.

examples.text: Eles falaram sobre os índios do Brasil.
examples.trans: They spoke about the Indigenous peoples of Brazil.

examples.text: A história do índio está no livro.
examples.trans: The story of the Indigenous person is in the book.

meanings.note: A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.
3rd plural consideram without a subject means 'people/they consider'.

examples.text: Eles não consideram isso um problema.
examples.trans: They do not consider that a problem.
I consider you a great friend.

meanings.note: Followed by an infinitive for your own wish (quero saber) or que + subjunctive for someone else (quero que você entre).

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

meanings.note: Head of state or of an organization.

examples.text: Ele quer ser presidente da república.
examples.trans: He wants to be president of the republic.

meanings.note: Used as a noun (o brasileiro = the Brazilian citizen) or as a nationality adjective.

examples.text: Você falou o que o brasileiro queria ouvir.
examples.trans: You said what the Brazilian wanted to hear.

examples.text: O povo brasileiro é muito criativo.
examples.trans: The Brazilian people are very creative.

meanings.note: Formed from real + -mente.

examples.text: Agora realmente o senhor passou dos limites.
examples.trans: Now you really crossed the line.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine singular; plural imprevisíveis.
Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.

meanings.note: Placed after a singular noun (problema nenhum) for emphatic negation: no problem at all.

examples.trans: There is no problem at all.

examples.text: Não tenho nenhum jeito de sair.
examples.trans: I have no way at all to leave.

meanings.note: Não tem jeito means there is no way.

examples.text: Não tem nenhum jeito de resolver isso?
examples.trans: Is there no way at all to solve this?

meanings.note: In Brazilian politics, ser cassado(a) means having one's electoral mandate revoked by the legislature or courts.

examples.trans: You have to get stripped of office.

meanings.note: Plural animais changes -al to -ais.

examples.trans: Talk about animals in the interview.

meanings.note: Nasal interjection expressing bewildered surprise or asking someone to repeat.
In até logo it looks ahead to the next meeting. The phrase is added as the lesson farewell, not quoted from the selected source window.
